body:
Problem: Floating windows lack mouse drag support for resizing and moving.

Solution:
Add a `mousedrag` option to `nvim_open_win()`, with three booleans that
default to false:
- `title`: drag the title or footer text to move the window.
- `content`: drag the text area to move the window. Dragging there no
  longer selects text.
- `border`: drag a border or a corner to resize the window.
  
Fix #35669

![test4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50547ffe-5d7c-43a4-8943-d71701552a90)

comment_data.body:
this is a complex interaction of 3 new flags. the docs are hinting that it's complex already, but we have the chance now to make a simple interface instead.

(there is also an existing `mouse` flag which decides whether mouseevents pass-through. that sure seems relevant... unfortunately it's a boolean instead of a string like `passthrough|normal|drag`.)

possible idea:

```lua
mousedrag = { title:'move'|'resize', border:'move'|'resize', content:'move'|'resize' }
```

but i think it could be even simpler:


```lua
mousedrag = { title:boolean, border:boolean, content:boolean }
```

- if `content=true` then content-drag *moves* the window.
- if `border=true` then border-drag *resizes*.
    - if `title=false/nil` then the title counts as a "border".
- if `title=true` then title-drag *moves* the window.

get_bordertext_col is similar https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/c4af59647fbd1f6fbf75abe8eb3d4b114ab66b1b/src/nvim/grid.c#L1127


anyways, this is about positioning, not mouse-specific. should live in src/nvim/api/win_config.c i guess, or maybe grid.c

sure seems like this could take a position parameter and then wouldn't need to be mouse-specific.

please design functions with generalization in mind. is there not any similar function already?
is this actually mouse-specific or is it more like "move a window"? and don't we have any existing function that repositions a float window already?
new enums should follow our naming conventions https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/c4af59647fbd1f6fbf75abe8eb3d4b114ab66b1b/runtime/doc/dev_style.txt#L458-L460
renamed to win_float_drag_at, and moved to winfloat.c. mouse.c just passes mouse_row/mouse_col in.

It's really about moving/resizing a window, not the mouse, so `win_float_drag()` belongs in winfloat.c.

`win_config_float()` is just the low-level applier. `win_float_drag()` computes the new geometry and hands it off, so it's not duplicating anything.

On keeping `border-as-move`: only border is ambiguous between `move/resize`, title/content are always move. 
```
mousedrag = { title:bool, content:bool, border: 'none'|'move'|'resize' }
```
border as a tri-state ennum. Keeps `title/content` as simple bools, only makes the genuinely ambiguous region richer. Avoids both the full string version's verbosity and the flag-coupling from my current impl.
If you'd rather just drop border-as-move and go pure bool `{title, border, content}`, that's a trivial change from this (border enum  -> bool). I lean toward keeping it as the enum since the cost is low and it covers borderless-draggable floats, but your call.

comment_data.body:
really need to think about names. not sure about this one yet.

thinking about names helps find better abstractions and reveals shared concepts (code re-use).


```suggestion
int win_float_drag_action(win_T *wp, int row, int col)
```

the name just above this is a clue that `float_edge_type` is not a good name.

```suggestion
  static int floatwin_drag = 0;
```
why do these need to be stored...? why can't the caller below calculate these

> If there's no title or footer and content = false that mean the user wants to stay in Visual mode for mouse selection, then how would they move the window?


they can't, because the winconfig disabled everything. and the workaround is either:

- enable a title (it could be empty)
- enable `content:true`. mouse-visual is not worth complexity, just use `v`.

all of the fields should be boolean.
